content.comment_body: Why am I unable to connect IM1 with SF01? What steps are needed to resolve this issue?

Hello, please provide a screenshot so it is clearer what you are trying to connect. I see you did so in your edit. You can use IM only after the IM coil. Also, if you use Function Block Diagram programming, handling IM is not a concern. Best regards, [user_name]
Hi, it is recommended to use a FLAG M1 instead of an internal flag IM1, making it easier to manage in FBD. I illustrated this in the attached image.
Internal flags or markers can increase the number of digital outputs, especially in lengthy programs.
This is part of the problem. I am using the [product_name] standard module with [article_no] and cannot find the flag option. Why am I unable to connect T03 and SF01 as shown in the attached image?
Hello, [article_no] is quite old. Have you tried using output or function instead?
I would like to reset the SF01 function, but I am unsure how to do it.

Hello, Using [product_name] with [article_no], only constants/connectors like Input, Output, Status 1 (high), and Status 0 (low) are available — flags are not supported. Flags are available in [article_no] and newer. You can check this within [product_name] Soft Comfort: Tools > Select Hardware (Ctrl+H). This means IM1 cannot be used as a connector in your version. However, you can use Q1, Q2, and so on—please refer to the attached image. Hope this helps!

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering difficulties connecting certain logic elements due to hardware and software limitations of an older [product_name] module. The lack of internal flags/markers in earlier versions, combined with ambiguous documentation about available connectors, has led to confusion and user frustration. Workarounds are being discussed, but the absence of support for flags/markers in specific models is limiting functionality.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to use internal flags or markers as connectors and reset function blocks easily, regardless of the hardware version they own.
